title: Generic operational Workbench specimen
hypothesis: A compact, flat, border-led presentation can support repeated inspect, compare, decide, and act work while keeping selection, evidence, decisions, and completion adjacent.

boundary: This specimen does not modify surface classification or recommendation.
The specimen remains evidence; the canonical registry and generated public export own the supported profile.
The profile must not activate from a low-evidence fallback surface id.
External design-system adapters remain authoritative and receive no implicit JudgmentKit fallback.
No product-specific workflow model, graph vocabulary, or source asset was copied from the directional reference.

activity_model.activity: Repeatedly review bounded requests and leave actionable handoffs.
activity_model.objective: Inspect one request, compare its evidence, choose an outcome, and preserve a reason for the next owner.
rules_and_rituals: show why an outcome is unavailable
keep the selected request and decision context together

division_of_labor.surface: organize requests, expose relevant evidence, constrain unsupported outcomes, and preserve the handoff
division_of_labor.human: interpret the evidence, choose the outcome, and supply the reason

activity_model.diagnostic_disclosure: The two diagnostic controls appear only in the separate specimen bar.

interaction_contract.user_goal: Move repeated requests forward without losing selection context or reconstructing evidence.
primary_decisions: whether available evidence supports a handoff
which outcome and reason should be recorded
make_easy: leave a receipt with the next owner
meaningful_state_changes: outcome selected or unavailable with reason
interaction_contract.completion_knowledge: The user knows which request was handled, why, what outcome was recorded, and who owns the next step.

regions.responsibility: Selected request context and decision framing
Adjacent comparison of supporting items, availability, and reasons
Bounded outcome selection, one primary completion action, disabled reasons, and receipt

visual_contract.typography: compact system-stack roles with tabular numeric metadata

icons.usage: inline SVG paired with visible status text and reason

responsive_contract.desktop: Queue, detail/evidence, and decision/handoff remain simultaneously visible.
responsive_contract.mobile: One region is visible at a time with an explicit Queue to Detail to Decision navigation sequence.

states.expectation: Queue, selected detail, evidence, decisions, and handoff action are available.
Every work region names what is loading while controls that depend on current data are unavailable.
The error is announced, retry is available, and no decision can be completed.
The clear queue, missing selection, and no-decision states are distinct.
Ready-to-handoff is disabled with an adjacent evidence-based reason while other outcomes remain available.
All interactive controls show a visible focus indicator in light, dark, and forced-colors modes.

states.entry: Select RQ-4798 or complete an available handoff
states.expectation: The decision form is replaced by a status receipt naming the outcome and next owner.

states.entry: Search for a string not in the fixture
states.expectation: The queue reports zero matches without erasing the selected request context.

qa_expectations.expectation: At 1280x800 and wider, the three regions remain visible without clipped content or actions.
At 390x844 and 320 CSS pixels wide, the explicit three-step flow has no horizontal page scrolling.
System follows prefers-color-scheme and explicit light or dark overrides it without token drift.
Every operation has a keyboard path, focus order preserves the workflow, and focus remains visible and unobscured.
Queue selection, appearance/state controls, decisions, disabled reasons, alerts, status updates, and receipt semantics are exposed.
Every status has an icon, text label, and visible reason.
Unsupported outcomes are disabled with reasons; the single primary action requires an available outcome and leaves a receipt.
Selection, controls, focus, status, and action boundaries remain perceivable.
At 200 percent zoom and 320 CSS pixel width, content reflows without two-dimensional scrolling.
Normal text meets 4.5:1, large text meets 3:1, and meaningful custom boundaries and icons meet 3:1, backed by computed browser evidence.
Long titles, names, evidence reasons, and 240-character notes wrap without collision or hidden controls.

post_promotion_requirements: Validate reusable component candidates with a second domain-neutral fixture and at least two genuinely different domain consumers.
Keep automatic and exact selection blocked for a low-confidence fallback without independently supplied Workbench evidence.
Keep automatic selection isolated from external design systems and reject exact JudgmentKit profile selection under external authority.
Require each rendered consumer to pass applicable desktop, mobile, keyboard, automated accessibility, forced-colors, zoom, overflow, contrast, and content-stress QA in light and dark modes.
limitations: This is a static specimen, not a renderer or reusable component package.
Fixture data and completed decisions reset on reload.
Search, save, and handoff behavior have no external side effects.
The visible appearance toggle is specimen instrumentation, not a production default.

Browser and computed-contrast evidence is partial; assistive-technology, forced-colors, automated accessibility, visual-regression, and second-domain evidence remain open for rendered consumers or later component expansion.
